entries.0d802c88db78775a: A segment of the Product Transport Business that owns and operates car carriers and also conducts logistics business, including operation of container terminals, air and sea freight forwarding, land transport, warehousing and heavy cargo transport. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥587,887 million, accounting for most of the Product Transport Business. The automobile transport business of this segment, together with the Energy Business, contributed to the group's overall revenue growth. Demand for finished vehicle transport was firm, but vessel deployment efficiency was constrained by port congestion and the situation in the Middle East. In the port business, handling volumes at domestic container terminals were generally firm, and handling volumes at the Vietnamese terminal in which the company invests were also firm. The segment was renamed from “Car Carrier, Port & Logistics Business” in the fiscal year ended March 2026; the change has no effect on the figures.

The core subsidiary Daibiru Corporation benefited from its existing office and commercial buildings and from the newly acquired 135 King Street in Australia and Capital House in the United Kingdom. The number of employees was 1,255 as of March 31, 2026.

Principal affiliates are Mitsui O.S.K. Bay Links Co., Ltd., Nihon Eisen Co., Ltd., Green Kaiji Co., Ltd., Green Shipping Co., Ltd. and Mitsui O.S.K. Techno Trade Co., Ltd. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥58,252 million (108.5% year on year), ranking 5th among the 6 business categories. Tugboat operations saw steady work volumes. The number of employees was 483 as of March 31, 2026.

entries.91913c1472223473: This segment within the Wellbeing Life Business operates ferries carrying passengers and cargo and owns and operates cruise ships to run the cruise business. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥73,385 million, the largest within the Wellbeing Life Business. Shosen Mitsui Sunflower Co., Ltd. saw fewer sailings and lower cargo volumes, but these were offset by strong passenger business centered on the Kansai route and by revised freight rates. In the cruise business, MITSUI OCEAN FUJI was out of service for repairs, and it took time to create demand.

In some projects of the Gas Infrastructure Business, operating efficiency declined due to equipment malfunctions.
entries.969ae5dfee7be848: Maritime Cargo Transport by Car Carriers
entries.a4acc831571d6cc2: A segment of the Energy Business consisting of maritime transport by crude oil tankers, product tankers, LPG carriers and chemical tankers, and the tank container business. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, crude oil tanker market conditions remained at high levels from September onward, when cargo volumes increased following the lifting of voluntary production cuts by OPEC+ countries. For product tankers, market conditions for large vessels were firm, while for LPG carriers, trade became more complex due to US port fee measures and US-China tariff issues, and ton-miles increased. For chemical tankers, market conditions softened due to uncertainty in the global economy.
entries.a693462da6657207: A business that, through its affiliates, conducts real estate business including land and building leasing and building management, passenger and cargo transport mainly in Pacific coastal waters and the Seto Inland Sea, and cruise business.
entries.ac5a2c67ccdc39e0: A business that owns and operates dry bulk carriers to provide global maritime cargo transport. Principal subsidiaries are Mitsui O.S.K. Dry Bulk, Ltd., MOL OCEAN BULK PTE. LTD. and GEARBULK HOLDING AG. In January 2025, the company made Gearbulk Holding AG (Switzerland) a consolidated subsidiary. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥455,734 million (98.9% of the previous year), the third largest of the 6 business segments. Capesize bulkers saw firm shipments of iron ore and bauxite from Western Australia and Brazil, and market conditions remained solid. Panamax and smaller vessels were supported by cargo movements of grain, coal and minor bulks. In the Gearbulk open hatch vessel business, demand for transport of pulp, the main cargo, softened, but contracts were secured for transport of aluminum and project cargo. Number of employees: 328 (as of March 31, 2026).
